title: Agentic AI Security Review Workflow — AT&T — AI Security & Governance Engineering (Jan 2026 – Present)
text: Architecture & Workflow Intake Collect structured information about the AI use case — data, models, users, tools, deployment environment, and intended actions. Validation Verify required fields, reject malformed inputs, and flag missing evidence before analysis begins. Specialized Review Agents Independently assess data privacy, security architecture, LLM/agent risk, access control, operational monitoring, and governance requirements. Evidence Grounding Link every finding to submitted architecture, data-flow information, and security-control evidence instead of allowing unsupported conclusions. Risk Aggregation Normalize findings, remove duplicates, assign severity, and identify control gaps. Escalation & Approval Route high-risk or low-confidence cases to human reviewers — final approval stays outside unrestricted model control.

title: Agentic AI Security Review Workflow — AT&T — AI Security & Governance Engineering (Jan 2026 – Present)
text: Reporting Generate an auditable review package, remediation tasks, status, exceptions, and operational metrics. Security Controls Least-Privilege Tool Access Separate identities for distinct workflow components, each scoped to only what it needs. Structured Schemas Allowlisted tools/actions and deterministic policy checks instead of free-form model authority. Human Approval Gates High-impact decisions and exceptions require human sign-off — the model recommends, it doesn't decide. Full Traceability Prompt, tool-call, evidence, decision, and output logging for audit. Adversarial Testing Prompt-injection and indirect-injection testing, including malicious instructions embedded in uploaded evidence. Data Handling Limits Sensitive-data handling requirements, output filtering, and limits on what context reaches the model.

title: Agentic AI Security Review Workflow — AT&T — AI Security & Governance Engineering (Jan 2026 – Present)

text: Self-Improving Mud Report Automation. NOV Inc. — IADC/SPE 230772, featured in Drilling Contractor. June 2025 – Dec 2025. Agentic AI GenAI Evaluation Published Research Turned a static-prompt PDF parser into a self-improving system — cutting prompt-development time from 960 minutes to 8.8. Daily mud reports arrive as multi-page PDFs with complex tables and layouts that vary across vendors and wells. The original system used static prompts — it worked on known formats, but had no way to measure accuracy or adapt to new templates. My Role Designed the core self-improvement logic and vendor-detection path. Built the prompt-generation, optimization, and dynamic prompt registry. Introduced the ground-truth evaluation database and accuracy scoring. Defined human review for new vendors and outliers.

title: Self-Improving Mud Report Automation — NOV Inc. — IADC/SPE 230772, featured in Drilling Contractor (June 2025 – Dec 2025)
text: End-to-End Workflow Ingestion Collect incoming mud-report PDFs from the approved enterprise source and associate them with report metadata. Extraction Preserve text, table structure, images, vendor names, API well numbers, and other key fields in an LLM-readable representation. Vendor Detection Determine whether a report belongs to a known vendor/template or represents an unfamiliar structure. Known-Vendor Path Retrieve the approved vendor-specific prompt from the dynamic prompt registry and run structured extraction. New-Vendor Path Activate prompt-generation and optimization agents that study historical examples and draft an initial vendor-specific prompt. Structured Parsing Convert the report into standardized fields suitable for centralized storage and downstream analytics. Ground-Truth Comparison Compare generated fields against records manually verified by a drilling engineer.

title: Self-Improving Mud Report Automation — NOV Inc. — IADC/SPE 230772, featured in Drilling Contractor (June 2025 – Dec 2025)
text: Accuracy Assessment Calculate field-level and report-level accuracy, identify missing/incorrect values, and classify error patterns. Controlled Self-Improvement Feed evaluation results back to the prompt agents — a candidate improvement is generated, retested, and stored only if it passes validation criteria. Human Approval & Monitoring Human review is retained for new vendors, structural changes, low-confidence outputs, outliers, and production exceptions. Why the Evaluation Database Mattered Without it, self-improvement would be unsafe to trust — a model could change a prompt and quietly reduce accuracy. Every candidate prompt had to beat the production prompt on human-verified records before it could replace it, with full rollback history. Risks Considered & Controls Prompt Injection Malicious instructions embedded in PDF text, tables, images, or engineering remarks.

title: Self-Improving Mud Report Automation — NOV Inc. — IADC/SPE 230772, featured in Drilling Contractor (June 2025 – Dec 2025)

text: Enterprise AI Email-Routing Automation. NOV Inc.. June 2025 – Dec 2025. Workflow Automation Threat Modeling OWASP LLM Top 10 Automated 50+ daily inbound inquiries at ~95% routing accuracy — without giving the model free rein over recipients. NOV received 50+ "Contact Us" inquiries per day that employees had to manually read and forward to the right team, costing 20+ hours a week and risking inconsistent or unsafe routing. My Role Designed the intent-based routing workflow and confidence thresholds. Threat-modeled prompt injection and sensitive-data exposure. Built destination allowlists so the model can't freelance. title: Enterprise AI Email-Routing Automation — NOV Inc. (June 2025 – Dec 2025)
text: Sanitize & Classify Classify untrusted content without treating the sender's text as trusted instructions. Context Retrieval Retrieve only the approved company information needed for routing. Routing Decision Generate a structured routing decision with destination, reason, and confidence. Rule Enforcement Apply deterministic business rules and destination allowlists. Escalation Route low-confidence or sensitive cases to a human rather than auto-forwarding. Monitoring Record the decision and outcome for quality review and troubleshooting. Prompt Injection Tested direct and indirect prompt injection embedded in message text. Destination Allowlists The model cannot select arbitrary recipients — routing is checked against deterministic rules.
